title: apis[].path carrying a snake_case path parameter — API_STANDARD.md §5's own worked example
coversRequirement: ADR 0012 — the apis[].path character class must admit '_', so snake_case path parameters are expressible
why: API_STANDARD.md §5 requires snake_case on the wire consistently and everywhere, and the path parameter carries the field name it names. Before ADR 0012 the character class omitted '_', so the standard's own worked example — /api/v1/orders/{order_id} — was rejected by the registry that is supposed to encode the standard, and the only paths the schema accepted were the ones the standard forbids. That is not a cosmetic mismatch: the cheapest way past a red light was to write {order-id}, putting a kebab-case parameter on the wire in a platform that mandates snake_case, and a grammar that only accepts non-conforming paths trains every App author to write non-conforming paths. This case pins the widened class so the defect cannot silently return in a later edit to the pattern.
notes: MUST BE ACCEPTED. Report side by side with adr0012-n1: this case alone going red means ADR 0012 is not implemented; both going green means the path grammar is not being enforced at all. Decidable by the schema alone — it is a plain grammar check on one string, with no cross-array join, so this is NOT a validator-layer case and a rejection here is a real schema defect. The path is /orders/{order_id}, the §5 example form. The manifest declares no Action at scope 'own', so no result is attributable to VAL-OWN or AZ7, and it is byte-identical to adr0012-n1 apart from the single apis[0].path string. The Action's exposure includes 'public' so that the 'public' surface declared in the apis entry is not an undeclared exposure — that consistency is not schema-enforced, and this fixture does not test it; it is set correctly only so the fixture is not quietly modelling a second defect while testing the first.
